page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top tier (top 10%). Large-block memory bandwidth for both read and write operations ranks in the top 25%, indicating efficient data throughput for memory-intensive operations. CPU-bound tasks, such as bzip3 decompression, also demonstrate strong multi-threaded performance. However, LLM inference tasks show limitations, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model falling into the bottom 25% performance category.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency compared to traditional x86 architectures for general-purpose workloads. The inclusion of 950 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance highly suitable for applications requiring low-latency scratch space or local caching. Recommended workloads include database operations, web serving, containerized microservices, and general-purpose application hosting where local high-speed storage and strong memory bandwidth are required.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by 16 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 64.0 GB of RAM and 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. The instance delivers strong memory performance, with its Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10% and large-block memory bandwidth in the top 25%. While single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks generally align with average mid-tier performance, its multi-threaded decompression and database operations show strong results. Lacking a GPU, it is not optimized for heavy machine learning tasks, as evidenced by lower LLM prompt processing speeds. However, its balanced resource allocation and high-speed local storage make it highly cost-efficient for database hosting, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
